*One merge-blocking issue* in `leaderboard-sort` (`17941bc`) vs `main` (`93d02a4`):

*P1 — Sorting silently loses score precision* — `src/rank.js:3`
`b.score - a.score` coerces the decimal strings to JavaScript Numbers, violating the existing arbitrary-precision score contract.

Reproduced with scores supplied in this order:
• `"9007199254740992"`
• `"9007199254740993"`

`rankings()` incorrectly leaves the lower score first, and `topN(entries, 1)` returns the wrong winner. Both strings round to the same Number, so the comparator treats them as tied.

*Recommended fix:* use the existing comparator: `.sort((a, b) => compareScore(b.score, a.score))`, and add a regression test covering these scores in both ranking and top-N.

All 3 existing tests pass, but the ranking test only uses small scores. No other concrete issues found. *I’d fix this before merging this afternoon.* No code changed.
